summary: LLM inference costs are dominated by token volume, with flagship models charging 4-5x more for output than input tokens — a workload that costs $3,250/month on a flagship model can drop to $195 on a budget tier for identical tokens. Combining prompt caching (up to 90% savings on repeated prefixes), semantic caching (documented 73% total cost reductions, e.g. $47,000 to $12,700 monthly), model routing, and output constraints routinely cuts production LLM spend by 50-80% without sacrificing quality. Most teams can implement the highest-leverage techniques in a few weeks with one or two engineers.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (Prefix/KV Caching)
techniques.description: Stores the computed key-value tensors behind a repeated, static prompt prefix (system prompts, RAG knowledge bases, few-shot examples) so providers charge dramatically less for the cached portion. The saving is structural, not a quality trade-off, but the static part must stay byte-identical and be ordered first in the prompt.
techniques.savings: 41-80% cost reduction; up to 90% on cached prefixes; 13-31% faster time-to-first-token
techniques.example: Place a 10,000-token shared system prompt at the very start of every request so Anthropic/OpenAI cache the prefix; only the user's dynamic question is billed at full rate. Avoid putting volatile tool results inside the cached prefix, which can paradoxically increase latency.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Uses vector embeddings to match new requests against previously answered ones by meaning rather than exact text, returning the cached response and eliminating the entire LLM call. Complementary to prompt caching, which only discounts repeated tokens within a call.
techniques.savings: 73% total cost reduction typical (cache hit rates jumping from ~18% to 67-90%)
techniques.example: Run user queries through an embedding model and a vector store (Redis/GPTCache); if 'How do I reset my password?' is semantically within threshold of a cached 'password reset' answer, serve the cached response with zero API spend.

techniques.name: Model Routing / Cascading
techniques.description: Routes each request to the cheapest model capable of handling it, reserving flagship models for genuinely hard queries. Simple classification or confidence-based cascades send the bulk of traffic to budget-tier models.
techniques.savings: 50-90% cost reduction (budget tier is ~16x cheaper for identical token counts)
techniques.example: Route 70% of traffic to GPT-4o-mini, 25% to a mid-tier model, and only 5% to GPT-4o after a lightweight classifier judges complexity, keeping quality where it matters while slashing average cost per request.

techniques.name: Output Constraints / Verbosity Control
techniques.description: Explicitly limits response length via max_tokens, structured output schemas, and prompts that penalize verbosity. Since output tokens cost 4-5x input tokens, trimming them yields outsized savings.
techniques.savings: 50% fewer output tokens; CROP method achieved 80.6% cost reduction by penalizing verbose outputs
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and instruct 'Answer in at most 3 bullet points, no preamble' to stop the model from generating long, expensive explanations nobody reads.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Reduces the token count of prompts by removing redundancy, abbreviating instructions, and compressing context (e.g. LLMLingua-style compression of RAG chunks) while preserving semantic meaning.
techniques.example: Pass RAG retrieved passages through LLMLingua to drop filler words and low-information tokens, shrinking a 20,000-token context to ~14,000 tokens before sending it to the model.

techniques.name: Context Engineering & RAG Tuning
techniques.description: Retrieves and injects only the most relevant chunks instead of dumping entire documents, tuning chunk size, top-k, and reranking to minimize context tokens without losing answer quality.
techniques.example: Lower top-k from 10 to 4 chunks and add a reranker so only the highest-relevance passages reach the model, cutting input tokens while improving answer precision.

techniques.name: Session Context Management
techniques.description: Manages conversation history actively by summarizing or truncating older turns rather than resending the full transcript each turn, preventing token counts from growing unboundedly in multi-turn chat.
techniques.savings: Substantial token reduction in long chatbot sessions (grows with conversation length)
techniques.example: After 10 turns, replace the raw chat history with a 200-token running summary plus the last 2 messages, so each new request stays lean instead of resending thousands of tokens.

techniques.name: Multi-Tier Caching Strategy
techniques.description: Layers exact-match caching, semantic caching, and session context management together so each request is first checked for an identical hit, then a semantic match, before ever reaching the model.
techniques.savings: Combined 73-80% cost reduction in chatbot deployments
techniques.example: Front your chatbot with exact-match cache (hash lookup) → semantic cache (vector match) → prompt-cached LLM call, so only truly novel questions incur full model cost.

techniques.name: Code Mode for Agentic Workloads
techniques.description: For agents running across multiple MCP servers/tools, letting the model emit code that orchestrates tool calls rather than round-tripping each tool result through the context window dramatically cuts input tokens.
techniques.savings: Up to an order-of-magnitude (10x) reduction in input tokens for agentic workloads
techniques.example: Instead of feeding every tool's JSON output back into the prompt, have the agent write a short script that calls the MCP tools and returns only the final distilled result to the model.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library that stores LLM responses and serves cache hits via embedding similarity, integrating with OpenAI, LangChain and vector stores.
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open-source (self-hosted; you pay only for underlying infra)

tools.name: Redis / Redis LangCache (Semantic Cache)
tools.description: Vector-based semantic cache built on Redis that matches queries by meaning to cut API calls and latency; widely used as the caching layer in production chatbot stacks.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS/Community; Redis Cloud paid tiers from ~$5/month, enterprise usage-based

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK for 100+ LLM providers offering caching, model routing, fallbacks, and spend tracking behind a single OpenAI-compatible API.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; LiteLLM Enterprise from ~$250/month with SSO, budgets and support

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing caching, cost tracking, rate limiting, and request logging via a drop-in proxy.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (up to 10k requests/month); paid plans from $20/month, enterprise custom

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: Popular framework for building LLM apps with built-in LLM caching (in-memory, SQLite, Redis, GPTCache), prompt management, and RAG components.

tools.name: Bifrost
tools.description: High-performance LLM gateway that pairs semantic caching with provider-native prompt caching and routing; commonly used in production cost-optimization stacks for 2026.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source core free; managed/enterprise pricing on request

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression tool that uses a small model to drop low-information tokens, shrinking prompts (notably long RAG context) by up to 20x with minimal quality loss.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway offering semantic caching, routing, load balancing, guardrails, and cost observability across multiple providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free developer tier; paid plans from ~$49/month, enterprise custom

quick_wins: Enable provider-native prompt caching and reorder prompts so the static system prompt/RAG context comes first — up to 90% savings on repeated prefixes with zero quality change.
Set strict max_tokens limits and add 'be concise, no preamble' instructions to cut expensive output tokens (which cost 4-5x input) by roughly 50%.
Add a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of your chatbot to lift cache hit rates from ~18% to 60-90% and eliminate duplicate calls entirely.
Route traffic through a gateway (LiteLLM/Helicone) and send the majority of simple requests to a budget-tier model, which is ~16x cheaper for identical token counts.
Trim RAG context by lowering top-k and adding a reranker so only the most relevant chunks reach the model, cutting input tokens 30-60%.
